title: Saratoga Club and Casper Holstein as boss
summary: Barbarin describes the basement club on Lenox Avenue and Holstein as a kind employer who paid on Mondays, and the story of his kidnapping.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: That was on Lenox between 139 and 40.
What kind of a place was it?

All this place happened to be down in the basement, you know? It was down in the basement. I had a full show there. It was a good show. Casper Holstein, which was the proprietor, he was a very nice man. You didn't have to worry about your money. I mean, whether he did business or not, he always had a smile on his face. You see, if they wouldn't have many people all the week, he never tormented the band, say to the band, and, man, he's not playing. I mean, what's happening to the band, and what's this and what's that. Find all kind of excuses. On a Monday night, it was our pay night, and he'd come up to Emble Up and give Russell, give a little Russell Emble Up to pay us off, and with a big smile on his face. Never hear him complain. Never hear him complain. Never complain. He's a great man to work for. They kidnapped him one time. I don't know. Really? You see, yeah, yeah. He had a policy racket, you know, and they kidnapped him and kept him for about a couple of weeks. There was no way he was at. Look him find him. Detective looking all over for him. Had all the police force, I imagine, in New York looking for him, Casper Holstein. I think they gave the guys the money, though, and he didn't say anything. He saved his life. He never really said who he was. He knew the guys. So they had him someplace on it, some holes on it, some old building or something like that. So they treated him all right, but they wanted that ransom money. I forgot how much ransom money it was. I don't know if it was $2,000 or whatever. I can't recall. That's how it took a drag, huh? Maybe he was. That's Russell's arrangement, I know that. He's on Don, too. It's Russell's arrangement.
